advances:
The exact finite support-hexagon system is infeasible with
\[
\frac{W}{M_x}+\frac{H}{M_y}>\frac{5000}{291}.
\]
The proof is an analytic elimination which is independent of which of
the four horizontal/vertical maximum-chord branches is active.  It
also covers all ties, coincident southwest vertices, and horizontal or
vertical support-face strata.  This does not prove that an arbitrary
positive cell can be reduced to its support hexagon.

proof:
The cross products in (2) follow directly from the six successive
edge pairs.  Shoelace gives (3).  Convexity and the zero southwest
cell give a common finite positive support-slope parameter
\(\tau\) at the two inner trace endpoints.  At the lower cap, the
inner support line of slope parameter \(\tau\) and the outer endpoint
support line of slope \(1/\alpha\) enclose a triangle of normalized
area
\[
\frac{1}{2(\tau^{-1}+\alpha)}.
\]
The left-cap analogue has normalized area
\[
\frac{1}{2(\tau+\beta)}.
\]
Both physical cap areas equal \(c\), and normalized area is multiplied
by \(D\).  This proves (5), including \(\alpha=0\) or \(\beta=0\) by
the corresponding vertical or horizontal support-line limit.

For completeness, (5) implies (6), because
\[
R-\alpha\geq\frac1\tau>0,\qquad
R-\beta\geq\tau>0.
\]
Conversely, under (6), the choice
\(\tau=1/(R-\alpha)\) satisfies both inequalities in (5).
The area added to \(K\) by adjoining the origin is exactly the
possibly degenerate triangle with vertices
\[
(0,0),\quad(a,0),\quad(0,b),
\]
of area \(ab/2\).  Thus (7) is exactly the anchor bound supplied by
accepted fact `92a1b537d7e7876c`.

Horizontal section length is piecewise affine between the vertex
levels \(0,b,B,Y,H\), so its maximum occurs at one of those levels.
Direct interpolation on the edges from \((A,0)\) to \((W,Y)\), and
from \((0,B)\) to \((X,H)\), gives (8)-(10).  The vertical argument,
with the coordinate roles exchanged, gives (11)-(13).  This proves
the asserted finite branch list, including every equality stratum.

It remains to eliminate all branches at once.  Put
\[
L=T(2+\alpha+\beta),\qquad
q_x=\frac{G}{W}.
\]
The chord in (8) exists in every branch, so \(M_x\geq G\).  Also
\[
0<q_x\leq1,\qquad
1-q_x=\frac{\alpha(Y-B)}{W}.                               \tag{15}
\]
Since \(H\geq Y\) and \(X\leq W\),
\[
\beta=\frac{H-B}{X}\geq\frac{Y-B}{W},
\]
and hence
\[
\alpha\beta\geq1-q_x.                                     \tag{16}
\]

The area identity needed for the elimination is
\[
2T=A+B-1+GY+FX-(1-\alpha\beta)XY.                          \tag{17}
\]
Furthermore,
\[
F-(1-\alpha\beta)Y
=(H-Y)+\beta(W-X)\geq0.                                   \tag{18}
\]
Using \(X\geq A\) in (17), followed by
\[
G-A(1-\alpha\beta)=\alpha F,
\]
gives
\[
2T\geq A+B-1+FW.                                          \tag{19}
\]
Since \(A,B\geq1\), \(G\geq1+\alpha\), \(F\geq1+\beta\), and
\(W=G/q_x\), equation (19) yields
\[
2T\geq1+\frac{(1+\alpha)(1+\beta)}{q_x}.                   \tag{20}
\]

Write \(s_x=\sqrt{1-q_x}\), so \(0\leq s_x<1\).  From (16) and
arithmetic-geometric mean,
\[
\alpha+\beta\geq2s_x,\qquad
(1+\alpha)(1+\beta)\geq(1+s_x)^2.
\]
Multiplying (20) by \((2+\alpha+\beta)/2\) gives
\[
L\geq
\frac{2(1+s_x)}{1-s_x}.                                   \tag{21}
\]
In particular \(L\geq2\), and (21) implies
\[
s_x\leq\frac{L-2}{L+2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
q_x=1-s_x^2\geq\frac{8L}{(L+2)^2}.                         \tag{22}
\]

The same proof after exchanging the two coordinates, using
\[
q_y=\frac{F}{H},\qquad
G-(1-\alpha\beta)X=(W-X)+\alpha(H-Y)\geq0,
\]
gives
\[
q_y\geq\frac{8L}{(L+2)^2}.                                \tag{23}
\]
Since \(M_x\geq G\) and \(M_y\geq F\), equations (22)-(23) imply
\[
\frac{W}{M_x}+\frac{H}{M_y}
\leq\frac{(L+2)^2}{4L}
=\frac{L}{4}+1+\frac1L.                                   \tag{24}
\]
No choice of \(J_x,J_y\), and hence no maximum-chord branch, enters
this estimate.

Adding the two cap inequalities (5) and using
\(\tau+\tau^{-1}\geq2\) gives
\[
D\geq c(2+\alpha+\beta).
\]
Together with \(DT=p\), this is
\[
L\leq\frac{p}{c}=\frac{194}{3}.                            \tag{25}
\]
The function \(L/4+1+1/L\) is nondecreasing for \(L\geq2\).
Equations (24)-(25) therefore give
\[
\frac{W}{M_x}+\frac{H}{M_y}
\leq
\frac{194/3}{4}+1+\frac{1}{194/3}
=\frac{5000}{291}.
\]
This proves (14).  Notice that the algebra proves the claim on the
larger system obtained by omitting the anchor (7), so every anchor
boundary or degeneracy is automatically covered.

WolframScript 1.13.0 with local Wolfram kernel 14.3.0 for Mac OS X ARM
was used only as an exact algebra audit.  Over the rational function
field in symbolic \(A,B,X,Y,\alpha,\beta,r\), the closed query checked
that the difference in (17) expands to zero after
\(W=A+\alpha Y,\ H=B+\beta X\), that
\[
(1-r^2)-\frac{8L_0}{(L_0+2)^2}=0
\quad\text{for}\quad
L_0=\frac{2(1+r)}{1-r},
\]
and that the final rational constant equals \(5000/291\); all three
checks returned `True` with exact inputs.  Bounded floating-point
maximizations were exploratory only and supply no evidence.  Every
inequality and every boundary case is proved by the hand argument
above; no `Reduce`, `Resolve`, timeout, or numerical conclusion is
used.
statement:
Assume the Alternative 1 cell data of accepted fact
`bc026780453747b8`, and use the southwest-anchor conclusion of accepted
fact `92a1b537d7e7876c`.  Put
\[
p=\frac{97}{100},\qquad c=\frac{3}{200},\qquad
r_-=\frac{87-3\sqrt{65}}{388}.
\]
In the finite support-hexagon model, normalize the two positive
axis-trace lengths to one and put
\[
A=a+1,\qquad B=b+1,
\]
\[
K=\operatorname{conv}\{(a,0),(A,0),(W,Y),(X,H),(0,B),(0,b)\}.
\]
The rightmost and topmost listed points are distinct.  The exact order
constraints are
\[
a,b\geq0,\qquad A\leq X\leq W,\qquad B\leq Y\leq H,
\qquad (W-X)+(H-Y)>0.                                      \tag{1}
\]
With the vertices in the displayed cyclic order, the six consecutive
cross products are
\[
Y,\quad
(W-A)(H-Y)+Y(W-X),\quad
(W-X)(H-B)+X(H-Y),\quad
X,\quad a,\quad b.                                         \tag{2}
\]
Thus convexity means that all quantities in (2) are nonnegative.
Under (1) this is automatic, but the non-strict form in (2) records
all collinear support faces.  The only possible coincident consecutive
vertices are \((a,0)=(0,b)=(0,0)\); coincidence of \((W,Y)\) and
\((X,H)\) is excluded by (1).

The normalized area and the physical axis-scale product are
\[
T=|K|
=\frac{AY+WH-XY+XB-ab}{2}>0,\qquad
D=\frac{p}{T}.                                              \tag{3}
\]
Define the two outer endpoint slopes
\[
\alpha=\frac{W-A}{Y},\qquad
\beta=\frac{H-B}{X}.                                       \tag{4}
\]
The exact two-cap constraint is the existence of \(\tau>0\) such that
\[
D\geq2c\left(\frac1\tau+\alpha\right),\qquad
D\geq2c(\tau+\beta).                                       \tag{5}
\]
Equivalently, with \(R=D/(2c)=100D/3\), it is the finite
real-algebraic condition
\[
R>\alpha,\qquad R>\beta,\qquad
(R-\alpha)(R-\beta)\geq1.                                  \tag{6}
\]
The exact southwest-anchor constraint is
\[
D\left(T+\frac{ab}{2}\right)
=p+\frac{Dab}{2}
\leq\frac{9}{200r_-^2}.                                    \tag{7}
\]

The maximum horizontal chord is attained at a level in
\(\{0,b,B,Y,H\}\).  Put
\[
G=A+\frac{(W-A)B}{Y}=A+\alpha B.                            \tag{8}
\]
If \(H>B\), put
\[
J_x=W-\frac{X(Y-B)}{H-B}.                                  \tag{9}
\]
Then
\[
M_x=\max\{G,J_x\}\quad(H>B),\qquad
M_x=W=G\quad(H=B).                                         \tag{10}
\]
Indeed, the chord lengths at \(y=b,B,Y\) are respectively
\[
A+\frac{(W-A)b}{Y},\qquad G,\qquad J_x,
\]
the first is at most \(G\), and the remaining levels contribute no
larger value.  When \(b=0\), the levels \(0\) and \(b\) coincide and
the chord has length \(A\).  When \(Y=H>B\), (9) is the top-face
length \(W-X\).  When \(Y=B<H\), both (8) and (9) equal \(W\).

The maximum vertical chord is attained at a level in
\(\{0,a,A,X,W\}\).  Put
\[
F=B+\frac{(H-B)A}{X}=B+\beta A.                            \tag{11}
\]
If \(W>A\), put
\[
J_y=H-\frac{Y(X-A)}{W-A}.                                  \tag{12}
\]
Then
\[
M_y=\max\{F,J_y\}\quad(W>A),\qquad
M_y=H=F\quad(W=A).                                         \tag{13}
\]
When \(a=0\), the levels \(0\) and \(a\) coincide and the vertical
chord has length \(B\).  When \(X=W>A\), (12) is the right-face
length \(H-Y\).  When \(X=A<W\), both (11) and (12) equal \(H\).

Consequently the nondegenerate region \(H>B,\ W>A\) has exactly the
four closed maximum branches obtained by independently choosing
\(G\) or \(J_x\) in (10), and \(F\) or \(J_y\) in (13), with the
corresponding weak comparison.  Ties lie in both adjacent branches.
Equations (10) and (13) also give every denominator-degenerate
support-face stratum.

Every tuple satisfying (1)-(7) and (10), (13) obeys
\[
\frac{W}{M_x}+\frac{H}{M_y}\leq\frac{5000}{291}.             \tag{14}
\]
Hence the requested strict inequality is infeasible in every
maximum-chord branch.
